claims.text: The starting material consists of tungsten particles or connected tungsten regions with native oxide surfaces in a copper-matrix precursor.
A graded molybdenum interlayer a few nanometers thick can be deposited on tungsten particles by low-pressure CVD at 600–800 °C.
Copper infiltration at 1100–1200 °C under an inert atmosphere will avoid oxidation during fabrication.
A molybdenum interlayer on tungsten enhances copper wettability.
The molybdenum interlayer minimizes thermal-expansion mismatch at the tungsten–copper interface.
The molybdenum interlayer acts as a diffusion barrier that prevents microvoid nucleation.
The molybdenum interlayer prevents formation of deleterious intermetallic phases at the tungsten–copper interface.
The molybdenum coating reduces interfacial energy between tungsten and copper.
The molybdenum coating creates a controlled chemical gradient that promotes uniform melting and diffusion.
Particle surface coating can improve mixture uniformity and reduce pore formation in a composite.
The molybdenum coating mitigates tungsten–copper phase separation during processing.
The molybdenum coating mitigates phase separation during irradiation exposure.
Mo-coated tungsten composites will have a lower void fraction than composites made from uncoated tungsten powders.
Mo-coated tungsten composites will have stronger interfacial cohesion than uncoated tungsten composites.
Mo-coated tungsten composites will have higher thermal conductivity than uncoated tungsten composites.
Mo-coated tungsten composites will sustain greater mechanical durability under irradiation than uncoated tungsten composites.
Surface-coated reinforcement particles can exhibit improved density, hardness, fracture strength, and interfacial bonding relative to uncoated particles.
Molten-copper infiltration or spark-plasma sintering of uncoated tungsten powders typically produces phase separation, voids, and compromised interfacial contact.
The proposed processing temperatures remain below copper's boiling point.
Long-term molybdenum diffusion or interfacial instability under irradiation may limit performance.
